result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.k_corona()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Extract the k-corona subgraph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L16698-L16778){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.k_corona(k) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The k-corona is the subgraph induced by nodes that are in the k-core and have exactly `k` neighbors in the k-core. These are the "boundary" nodes of the k-core that would be removed first when computing the `(k+1)`-core. The k-corona helps identify nodes at the periphery of dense substructures, which is useful for understanding hierarchical organization and vulnerability analysis. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [k]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The core number. Nodes in the k-corona have coreness >= `k` and exactly `k` neighbors within the k-core. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : New graph containing only the k-corona nodes and their connecting edges. May be empty if no nodes satisfy the k-corona criteria. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - the k-corona is a subset of the k-shell (nodes with coreness exactly k) - nodes in the k-corona are those that would lose their k-core membership if any of their k-core neighbors were removed - the k-corona can be empty even when the k-core is non-empty - useful for identifying structurally vulnerable nodes in dense subgraphs ## Examples {.doc-examples} Find the 2-corona in a simple graph: ::: {#15685068 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec # Create a graph with a dense core and peripheral nodes g = ec.Graph() # Dense core: nodes 1, 2, 3 form a triangle g.add_node(label="1") g.add_node(label="2") g.add_node(label="3") g.add_edge("1", "2") g.add_edge("2", "3") g.add_edge("3", "1") # Add peripheral nodes g.add_node(label="4") g.add_node(label="5") g.add_edge("1", "4") g.add_edge("2", "5") # The 2-corona contains nodes in the 2-core with exactly 2 neighbors in 2-core corona_2 = g.k_corona(2) # Returns the number of nodes in the 2-corona corona_2.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: Analyze hierarchical structure: ::: {#26ad7970 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Build a graph and examine different corona levels g = ec.Graph() g.add_full_graph(5) # K5 complete graph # In K5, all nodes have degree 4, so they're in the 4-core # Each node has exactly 4 neighbors in the 4-core corona_4 = g.k_corona(4) # Returns 5 (all 5 nodes are in the 4-corona) corona_4.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 5 ``` ::: :::
